references.text: Jacob sent gifts (mincha) to his brother Esau to appease him, just as Ehud brought a gift to Eglon.
Jacob's sons brought a gift (mincha) to Joseph in Egypt, illustrating the custom of bringing gifts to rulers.
Some despised Saul and brought him no gifts (mincha), showing the importance of bringing gifts to kings in Israel.
The kings brought gifts (mincha) to Solomon, demonstrating how subordinates brought tribute to their superiors.
Hosea no longer sent tribute to the king of Assyria, illustrating the obligation to bring gifts to overlords.
Moab brought tribute to David, showing that the Moabites were accustomed to paying tribute to Israelite kings.
